newsitem.title: USA: Chase insurance sees potential for growth.
newsitem.headline: Chase insurance sees potential for growth.

text.p: Chase Manhattan Bank's insurance sales business expects premium volume in 1996 to reach between $800 million and $1 billion, the unit's chief executive.
About $400 million of that will come from the sale of annuities, said Dennis Kosovac, chief executive of Chase Insurance Agency Inc.
"I think we're well-positioned for growth," said Kosovac, who held a similar position with Chemical Bank for three years before Chemical merged with Chase.

Instead of seeking out new customers, banks like Chase hope to sell insurance as one of an array of financial service products to their long-standing customers, with whom they have strong relationships, he said.
And major commercial banks have reason to hope for success, he said.
A survey of Chase's commercial banking clients found that only a few rejected the idea of banks offering insurance.
In addition, a "sizable portion" of the companies frequently change insurance brokers as they shop around for the best deals.
And the critical reason for switching brokers was price, he said.
This, he said, means commercial banks don't have to break up close relations, giving them a better chance of entering the business.
"There appears to be a window open," he said.
Most of the remainder will come from the sale of life, disability and personal lines property and casualty insurance, said Kosovac, one of the speakers Monday at the Insurance Leadership Forum.

Commercial property and casualty insurance currently makes up only a very small portion of the unit's sales, he said at the conference, sponsored by the Council of Insurance Agents & Brokers and the Council of Insurance Company Executives.
He said his five-year business plan is to quadruple this year's results and become a major contributor to Chase's overall results.
